language: Chinese (simplified), with pinyin entry readings and Latin botanical names

regions.text: 【用法与用量】　内服：煎汤，0.3～1两。外用：研末调敷。
regions.translation: [Method and dosage]  Internally: decocted, 0.3 to 1 liang (about 9 to 30 g). Externally: ground to powder and applied mixed.

regions.text: 【宜忌】　肝虚及中气虚寒者忌服。
regions.translation: [Cautions]  Those with liver deficiency, or with deficiency-cold of the centre qi, should not take it.

regions.text: ①《本草汇言》：“肝虚内乏，中气虚寒者，不必需也。”
regions.translation: ① Collected Sayings on Materia Medica [Bencao huiyan]: “Where the liver is deficient and depleted within, and where the centre qi is deficient and cold, it is not needed.”

regions.text: ②《本经逢原》：“不可过服，过服令人凛凛恶寒，以其专削阳气也。”
regions.translation: ② Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica [Benjing fengyuan]: “It must not be taken to excess; taken to excess it makes a man shiver with aversion to cold, for it does nothing but pare away the yang qi.”

regions.text:
【选方】　①治阳厥怒狂：生铁落为饮。（《素问》生铁落饮）
②治暴怒发狂：铁落三钱，甘草一钱。煎汤饮。（《方脉正宗》）
③治贼风流痛关节不能转动：铁落炒热，投酒中饮之。（《本草汇言》）
④治小儿赤丹斑驳：铜、铁屎，以猪脂和敷之。（《千金方》）
regions.translation:
[Selected prescriptions]  ① For yang reversal with rage and mania: raw tie luo made into a drink. (the Raw Iron-flake Drink, sheng tie luo yin, of the Basic Questions [Suwen])
② For sudden rage breaking out into mania: tie luo, three qian, and liquorice, one qian. Decoct and drink. (Orthodox Lineage of Prescriptions and Pulses [Fangmai zhengzong])
③ For thief-wind wandering pain, with the joints unable to turn: tie luo roasted hot and dropped into wine, which is then drunk. (Collected Sayings on Materia Medica)
④ For red erysipelas in children, mottled and blotchy: copper and iron dross, mixed with lard and applied. (the Thousand Gold Pieces Prescriptions [Qianjin fang])

regions.text: 【各家论述】　《本草经疏》：“铁落，本出于铁，不离金象，体重而降，故《素问》有生铁落饮，以疗病狂怒者，云生铁落，下气疾也。又怒狂属肝气暴升，故取金气以制之也。其主气在皮肤中及除胸膈中热气，食不下，止烦者，皆制木散热之功也。《本经》又主风热，恶疮，疡疽疮痂疥者，皆肝心火热所致，辛平能除二经之火热，故主之也。苏恭以之炒热投酒中饮疗贼风痉，大明治惊邪癫痫，小儿客忤，并煎服之，悉此意耳。”
regions.translation: [Commentaries of the various authors]  Commentary on the Classic of Materia Medica [Bencao jingshu]: “Iron flakes, tie luo, come originally from iron and do not depart from the image of metal; heavy in substance, they descend. Hence the Basic Questions has the Raw Iron-flake Drink, with which to treat those sick with mania and rage, saying that raw tie luo brings the qi down swiftly. Again, rage and mania belong to a violent upsurge of liver qi, and so the qi of metal is taken to restrain it. That it governs qi lodged within the skin, that it removes heat qi in the chest and diaphragm with food not going down, and that it stops vexation, are all the merit of restraining wood and dispersing heat. As for the Classic of Materia Medica [Shennong bencao jing] further making it govern wind-heat, malign sores, and ulcers, abscesses, scabbed sores and scabies, these are all brought about by fire heat of the liver and the heart; being acrid and neutral it can remove the fire heat of those two channels, and therefore it governs them. Su Gong had it roasted hot and dropped into wine to be drunk, to treat thief-wind tetany; Da Ming treated fright evil and epilepsy, and ke wu in small children (fright from a visiting influence), in every case decocting it and taking it. All of this is entirely this same intent.”

regions.text: 【备考】　《唐本草》：“铁落是煅家烧铁赤沸，砧上煅之，皮甲落者也，《甲乙》子卷阳厥条言之。夫诸铁疗病，并不入丸、散，皆煮取浆用之，若以浆为铁落，钢生之汁，复谓何等。落是铁皮滋液，黑于余铁。陶谓可以染皂，云是铁浆，误矣。”
regions.translation: [Note]  Materia Medica of the Tang [Tang bencao]: “Tie luo is the scaly skin that falls away when the smith heats iron until it is red and seething and forges it on the anvil; the Jiayi, i.e. the Systematic Classic of Acupuncture and Moxibustion [Zhenjiu jiayi jing], speaks of it in the section on yang reversal in the zi fascicle. Now none of the various irons that treat disease is put into pills or powders; all are boiled and the liquor taken for use. If the liquor were taken for tie luo, then what should the fluid that comes from steel be called? Luo is the moist substance of the iron's skin, blacker than the rest of the iron. Tao [Hongjing] said it may be used to dye black, calling it iron liquor; this is a mistake.”

regions.text: 3813 铁锈 tiě xiù （《本草拾遗》）
regions.translation: 3813  Iron rust, tie xiu (from the Supplement to Materia Medica [Bencao shiyi])

regions.text: 【异名】　铁衣（《普济方》），铁线粉（《养生经验合集》）。
regions.translation: [Synonyms]  tie yi, “iron coat” (Prescriptions for Universal Relief [Puji fang]); tie xian fen, “iron-wire powder” (Collected Experiences in Nourishing Life [Yangsheng jingyan heji]).

regions.text: 【基原】　为铁露置空气中氧化后生成的红褐色锈衣。
regions.translation: [Source]  The reddish-brown coat of rust formed when iron is left standing in the air and oxidises.

regions.text: 【炮制】　《日华子本草》：“煅后飞，淘去粗赤汁，烘干用。”
regions.translation: [Preparation]  Rihuazi's Materia Medica [Rihuazi bencao]: “Calcine it, then levigate it in water; rinse away the coarse red liquid, and bake it dry for use.”

regions.text: 【性味】　①《本草经疏》：“味辛苦，气寒。”
regions.translation: [Flavour and nature]  ① Commentary on the Classic of Materia Medica: “Acrid and bitter in flavour, cold in qi.”

regions.text: ②《本经逢原》：“辛，寒，无毒。”
regions.translation: ② Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica: “Acrid, cold, non-poisonous.”

regions.text: 【归经】　《本草经解》：“入手太阴肺、足阳明胃。”
regions.translation: [Channel entered]  Explanation of the Classic of Materia Medica [Bencao jingjie]: “It enters the hand taiyin lung and the foot yangming stomach.”

regions.text: 【功用主治】　清热解毒，镇心平肝。治疔疮肿毒，口疮，重舌，疥癣，烫伤，毒虫螫伤，痫病。
regions.translation: [Actions and indications]  Clears heat and resolves toxin; settles the heart and calms the liver. Treats boils with toxic swelling, mouth sores, double tongue (swelling beneath the tongue), scabies and tinea, scalds, stings by poisonous insects, and epilepsy.

regions.text: ①《本草拾遗》：“主恶疮疥癣，和油涂之。蜘蛛虫等咬，和蒜磨敷之。”
regions.translation: ① Supplement to Materia Medica: “Chiefly for malign sores, and for scabies and tinea — mix it with oil and smear it on. For bites by spiders and other insects, grind it with garlic and apply it.”

regions.text: ②《日华子本草》：“治痫疾，镇心，安五脏。能黑鬓发。”
regions.translation: ② Rihuazi's Materia Medica: “Treats epilepsy, settles the heart, and quiets the five viscera. It can blacken the hair of the temples and of the head.”

regions.text: ③陶华：“铁锈水和药服，性沉重，最能坠热开结。”
regions.translation: ③ Tao Hua: “Iron-rust water, taken mixed with the medicine, is heavy and sinking in nature, and is best able to bring heat down and to open up bindings.”

regions.text: ④《纲目》：“平肝坠热，消疮肿，口舌疮。醋磨涂蜈蚣咬。”
regions.translation: ④ The Gangmu, i.e. the Compendium of Materia Medica [Bencao gangmu]: “Calms the liver and brings heat down; disperses sores and swellings, and sores of the mouth and tongue. Ground with vinegar and smeared on for centipede bites.”

regions.text: ⑤《本草汇言》：“解疔毒，消恶疮，退风癣，散脚气壅肿。《嘉祐方》治伤寒热实结胸，磨水入承气汤服之。”
regions.translation: ⑤ Collected Sayings on Materia Medica: “Resolves the toxin of boils, disperses malign sores, drives back wind tinea, and dissipates the congested swelling of jiao qi (beriberi). The Jiayou Prescriptions [Jiayou fang] treats cold damage with heat-repletion binding in the chest: grind it with water, add it to the Chengqi decoction, and take.”

regions.text: ⑥《本经逢原》：“妇人产后阴挺不收，和冰片研水服之。蠼螋、蜈蚣咬，和蒜涂之。”
regions.translation: ⑥ Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica: “For prolapse of the uterus in a woman after childbirth, where it will not draw back in, grind it with borneol in water and take it. For bites of the earwig and the centipede, mix it with garlic and smear it on.”

regions.text: ⑦《医林纂要》：“补心宁神，解毒除热。朽铁上赤衣，涂漆疮。”
regions.translation: ⑦ Essentials Compiled from the Forest of Medicine [Yilin zuanyao]: “Supplements the heart and quiets the spirit; resolves toxin and eliminates heat. The red coat on decayed iron is smeared on lacquer sores.”

regions.text: 【用法与用量】　外用：研末撒或调敷。内服：研末水调。
regions.translation: [Method and dosage]  Externally: ground to a powder and sprinkled on, or mixed and applied. Internally: ground to a powder and mixed with water.

regions.text: 【选方】　①治疔疮：用多年墙内或泥土中锈钉，洗净，以灰火内煅，入醋内淬，待冷，用刀刮钉锈，又于火内煅红入醋淬，仍前刮末，再三如此煅淬，刮末用纱帛细罗包裹。遇人有此证，略将疮口拨开，挑药末在内，不以是为膏。（《普济
regions.translation: [Selected prescriptions]  ① For boils: take rusty nails that have lain for many years inside a wall or in the earth, wash them clean, calcine them in an ash fire, quench them in vinegar, and when they are cold scrape the rust off the nail with a knife; then calcine them red in the fire again and quench them in vinegar, scraping off the powder as before, and calcine and quench them in this way over and over. Scrape off the powder and wrap it in fine gauze silk. When you meet someone with this complaint, open the mouth of the sore a little, pick up some of the powder and put it inside, and do not make it up into a salve. (Prescriptions for Universal
Relief) [the tail of the source citation broken at the foot of the left column]

regions.text:
②治疔肿：铁衣末，以人乳和敷之。（《普济方》）
③治脚腿红肿，热如火炙，俗名赤游风：铁锈水涂解之。（《圣济方》）
④治重舌肿胀：铁锈锁烧红，打下锈，研末，水调二钱噙咽。（《生生编》）
⑤治汤火伤疮：青竹烧油，同铁锈搽之。（《积德堂经验方》）
⑥治风瘙瘾疹：铁锈磨水涂之。（《濒湖集简方》）
⑦治内热遗精：铁锈末，冷水服一钱，三服止。（《活人心统》）
regions.translation:
② For boils with swelling: powdered tie yi, mixed with human milk and applied. (Prescriptions for Universal Relief)
③ For redness and swelling of the feet and legs, hot as if scorched with fire, commonly called “red roving wind”: apply tie xiu water to it, and this resolves it. (the Sagely Benefaction Prescriptions [Shengji fang])
④ For double tongue with swelling and distension: heat a rusty iron lock red-hot, knock the rust off it, grind the rust to a powder, mix two qian (about 6 g) with water, hold it in the mouth and swallow it. (the Compilation on Fostering Life [Shengsheng bian])
⑤ For sores from scalds and burns: burn green bamboo for its oil, and rub it on together with tie xiu. (the Tried Prescriptions of the Hall of Accumulated Virtue [Jidetang jingyan fang])
⑥ For wind-itch and nettle rash: grind tie xiu in water and apply it. (Binhu's Collected Simple Prescriptions [Binhu jijian fang])
⑦ For seminal emission from internal heat: powdered tie xiu, one qian (about 3 g) taken in cold water; three doses will stop it. (the Comprehensive Guide to Saving Lives [Huoren xintong])

regions.text: 【各家论述】　《本草经疏》：“铁锈，其味辛苦，气寒。恶疮疥癣，湿热所生；蜘蛛虫咬，毒气伤血，辛苦能除湿热，寒能解热毒气，故主之也。又秘法，取露天入土者，研极细，同蟾酥、脑、麝，以金针刺入疔疮中，令至根，然后以药塞入，能拔疔根。”
regions.translation: [Commentaries of the various authors]  Commentary on the Classic of Materia Medica: “Iron rust, tie xiu, is acrid and bitter in flavour, cold in qi. Malign sores, scabies and tinea are produced by damp-heat; when spiders and such insects bite, the toxic qi damages the blood. The acrid and bitter can eliminate damp-heat, and the cold can resolve the qi of heat-toxin; hence it governs these. There is also a secret method: take a piece that has lain in the open and then gone into the earth, grind it extremely fine, and combine it with toad venom, borneol and musk; drive a golden needle into the boil so that it reaches the root, then stuff the medicine in — it can draw out the root of the boil.”

regions.text: 3814 铁精 tiě jīng （《本经》）
regions.translation: 3814  Iron essence, tie jing (from the Classic of Materia Medica)

regions.text: 【异名】　铁精粉（《子母秘录》），铁花（《纲目》）。
regions.translation: [Synonyms]  tie jing fen, “iron-essence powder” (Secret Records of Mother and Child [Zimu milu]); tie hua, “iron flower” (the Gangmu).

regions.text: 【基原】　为炼铁炉中的灰烬。
regions.translation: [Source]  The ash from an iron-smelting furnace.

regions.text: 【性味】　辛苦，平。
regions.translation: [Flavour and nature]  Acrid and bitter, neutral.

regions.text: ①《本经》：“平。”
regions.translation: ① The Classic of Materia Medica: “Neutral.”

regions.text: ②《别录》：“微温。”
regions.translation: ② The Supplementary Records [Mingyi bielu]: “Slightly warm.”

regions.text: ③《本草汇言》：“味苦辛，气温，无毒。”
regions.translation: ③ Collected Sayings on Materia Medica: “Bitter and acrid in flavour, warm in qi, non-poisonous.”

regions.text: ④《本经逢原》：“小毒。”
regions.translation: ④ Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica: “Slightly poisonous.”

regions.text: 【功用主治】　镇惊安神，消肿解毒。治惊痫心悸，疔毒，阴肿，脱肛。
regions.translation: [Actions and indications]  Settles fright and quiets the spirit; disperses swelling and resolves toxin. Treats fright epilepsy and palpitation, the toxin of boils, genital swelling, and rectal prolapse.

regions.text: ①《本经》：“主明目。”
regions.translation: ① The Classic of Materia Medica: “Chiefly brightens the eyes.”

regions.text: ②《别录》：“疗惊悸，定心气，小儿风痫，阴㿉，脱肛。”
regions.translation: ② The Supplementary Records: “Treats fright palpitation, settles the heart qi, and treats wind epilepsy in children, genital swelling (yin tui), and rectal prolapse.”

regions.text: ③《本草汇言》：“拔疔毒。”
regions.translation: ③ Collected Sayings on Materia Medica: “Draws out the toxin of boils.”

regions.text: ④《本经逢原》：“破胃脘积血作痛。”
regions.translation: ④ Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica: “Breaks up accumulated blood in the stomach duct that causes pain.”

regions.text: ⑤《医林纂要》：“泄肺热，坠涌痰。”
regions.translation: ⑤ Essentials Compiled from the Forest of Medicine: “Drains lung heat and brings down welling phlegm.”

regions.text: 【用法与用量】　内服：煎汤或入丸、散。外用：调敷。
regions.translation: [Method and dosage]  Internally: decocted, or made up into pills or powders. Externally: mixed and applied.

regions.text:
【选方】　①治火热燔心，暴发惊狂如痫者：铁精一钱，甘草二钱。煎汁饮。（《至宝方》）
②治阴肿：铁精粉敷上。（《子母秘录》）
③治妇人阴挺出下脱：铁精细研，以羊脂调，布裹，炙令热，熨之，以瘥为度。（《圣惠方》）
④治小儿因痢肛门脱：铁精粉敷之。（姚和众）
⑤治蛇骨刺人毒痛：铁精如大豆者，以管吹疮内。（《补缺肘后方》）
regions.translation:
[Selected prescriptions]  ① For fire-heat scorching the heart, with sudden outbreaks of fright and mania resembling epilepsy: tie jing, one qian (about 3 g), and liquorice, two qian (about 6 g). Decoct and drink the liquid. (the Supreme Treasure Prescriptions [Zhibao fang])
② For swelling of the genitals: dust powdered tie jing over the part. (Secret Records of Mother and Child)
③ For prolapse of the uterus in a woman, where it protrudes and falls down: grind tie jing fine, mix it with mutton fat, wrap it in cloth, roast it until hot, and iron the part with it, keeping on until she is well. (the Sagely Benevolence Prescriptions [Shenghui fang])
④ For rectal prolapse in a child from dysentery: dust powdered tie jing on it. (Yao Hezhong)
⑤ For the poisonous pain of a snake's bone pricking a person: take tie jing the size of a soya bean and blow it into the wound through a tube. (the Supplemented Handy Prescriptions for Emergencies [Buque zhouhou fang])

regions.text: 【各家论述】　①《本草汇言》：“铁精，疗惊痫，安心气，拔疔毒，止小儿阴㿉脱肛之药也。因火盛气怯，而神情浮越不静者，服之立安。倘由劳倦神疲，气虚魄乱，神不守舍，以致惊痫烦溃者，非所宜用也。”
regions.translation: [Commentaries of the various authors]  ① Collected Sayings on Materia Medica: “Iron essence, tie jing, is a drug that treats fright epilepsy, quiets the heart qi, draws out the toxin of boils, and stops genital swelling and rectal prolapse in children. Where fire is exuberant and the qi timid, so that the spirit and mood float upward and will not be still, taking it settles them at once. But where it comes of toil and fatigue with a weary spirit, of qi deficiency with the po soul in disorder and the spirit not keeping to its dwelling, so that fright epilepsy and vexed derangement ensue, then it is not a fit thing to use.”

regions.text: ②《本经逢原》：“铁精，胃气虚寒人服之，往往有夺食发呃之虞，以纯阴镇摄太过，而伤犯阳和之气也。”
regions.translation: ② Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica: “Tie jing: when persons of deficient and cold stomach qi take it, there is often the danger of the appetite being taken away and hiccup set off, for a thing of pure yin settles and restrains to excess, and so injures and offends the qi of yang harmony.”

regions.text: 【备考】　陶弘景：“铁精，出煅灶中，如尘，紫色，轻者为佳。”
regions.translation: [Note]  Tao Hongjing: “Tie jing comes out of the forging hearth; it is like dust, purple in colour, and the light sort is the best.”

regions.text: 3815 铁马豆 tiě mǎ dòu （《滇南本草》）
regions.translation: 3815  Iron-horse bean, tie ma dou [Shuteria pampaniniana] (from Materia Medica of Southern Yunnan [Diannan bencao])

regions.text: 【异名】　黄花马豆（《滇南本草》），蝴蝶草（《昆明民间常用草药》）。
regions.translation: [Synonyms]  huang hua ma dou, “yellow-flowered horse bean” (Materia Medica of Southern Yunnan); hu die cao, “butterfly herb” (Common Folk Herbal Medicines of Kunming [Kunming minjian changyong caoyao]).

regions.text: 【基原】　为豆科植物毛宿苞豆的全草。
regions.translation: [Source]  The whole plant of the leguminous plant mao su bao dou (hairy shuteria).

regions.text: 【原植物】　毛宿苞豆 Shuteria pampaniniana Hand.-
regions.translation: [Botanical source]  Hairy shuteria, Shuteria pampaniniana Hand.- [the authority is completed as “Hand.-Mazz.” at the head of the following page]
